issues.desc: background.md Key Insights cites transition-orchestrator.ts:663 as the source for the retention claim "review rounds are per-entry" (inherited verbatim from docs/requirements/decisions/repro-first-gate-enforce-execution-plan.md Workstream 2, commit 23600eb 2026-07-18). In the current src file packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts (1041 lines, after the S1/B-d877 and W1/B-956f merges on 2026-07-19/23), line 663 falls inside an unrelated DONE pre-merge-gate comment block ("TEST->DONE: block A (done-oracle gate + F-020 stray-file dry-run ...)"). The actual per-entry review-round assignment (`story.currentReviewRound = now;`, inside the REVIEW-advance branch) is now at line ~773. The underlying architectural fact is verified true, but the pinned line citation has drifted and would mislead an implementer trying to verify/cite it directly -- which matters because this spec storys stated goal is to produce contracts the W2 implementation stories can cite section-by-section.

index.json description uses the term "ProofStory red_evidence gate" but "ProofStory" is never defined or expanded anywhere in background.md, index.json, checklist.json, or root CLAUDE.md (grep for ProofStory in CLAUDE.md returns zero matches). A fresh reader with no conversation history can infer from context that it is some gate/evidence-consuming subsystem, but the term itself is never spelled out or pointed at a source file.

background.md Solution Tradeoffs uses the jargon "Tier-C fence" ("no cryptographic receipt signing (Tier-C fence)") without defining what Tier-C refers to anywhere in the required-reading scope (background.md/index.json/checklist.json/CLAUDE.md). Only contextually inferable as some kind of scope boundary around cryptographic signing, not explicitly defined on first appearance.
